summary: Up here the city has spent a century un-making streets about as often as making them. It closed parts of Grand View Avenue in 1930, Stanyan Street and Mountain Spring Avenue in 1931, Acme Alley the same year, a length of Portola Drive that had been the Old Ocean House Road in 1949, portions of six more streets in 1951, Raccoon Drive in 2014 — and in 2025 it gave notice that it means to vacate parts of Christmas Tree Point Road and Twin Peaks Boulevard for a promenade. What did get built had to be blasted out: permission to explode blasts to run a sewer through rock on Romain Street in 1909, on Seward Street in 1916, at Romain and Corbett in 1927. In the 1950s the sewers arrived ahead of the houses — Clarendon Avenue was sewered before it was widened, to serve the Forest Knolls and Midtown Terrace subdivisions, and the water was pushed over the hill by a pump station near Olympia Way that the city reported in 2002 had outlived itself. In 1990 the Planning Commission turned down a use proposed for 445 Burnett Avenue and the Board granted it anyway, with conditions. The names keep moving as well: Falcon Avenue became part of Market Street in 1918, and in 2023 a stretch of Palo Alto Avenue became La Avanzada Street.
